papers.version_note: arXiv:2302.05970v1 (12 Feb 2023); text layer holds the paper once, 22 pages, formulas partly scrambled by extraction.
papers.what_it_is: A numerical method for recovering a Sturm-Liouville potential on a quantum tree graph from its Weyl matrix, combining leaf peeling with Neumann series of Bessel functions.
papers.why_not: The 'quantum graph' here is a metric graph carrying a Sturm-Liouville differential operator (a classical inverse spectral problem in applied mathematics). It involves no quantum computing, quantum machine learning, classical machine learning, finance or statistical evaluation method, so it fits none of the five contexts.
